name: Old Garton
title: Miller
examine: Flour in every crease of him. Forty years of turning grain to bread have ground the hurry out of the man entirely.
lines: Wheat comes in, flour goes out, and the pond does the pushing. Perfect arrangement until somebody rings a bell through it.
That ferry bell of Peld's rings on the wrong wind and scares my herons. I've told him. He rings it anyway. Boy's lucky I like him.
My knees know the rain three days out. Better than any sage, and they charge less.
